moderngov_api_recipe.what: Every Modern.Gov instance here exposes an XML web service that removes the need to scrape HTML to find the budget meeting.
moderngov_api_recipe.trick: The <meetingstatus> field names the budget meeting outright, for example 'Confirmed; Budget Council' (Lambeth), 'Confirmed; Budget Meeting' (Richmond), 'Confirmed; Budget' (Newham), 'Confirmed; Budget and Council Tax Setting Meeting' (Southwark). Feed the meeting id into /ieListDocuments.aspx?CId=<cid>&MId=<mid> to get the agenda and its attachment links.
moderngov_api_recipe.dates: sFromDate and sToDate are dd/mm/yyyy. ISO dates return an error, not an empty list.

shared_blocking_pattern: Eight of these sixteen boroughs' committee sites returned HTTP 403 with an x-azure-ref header to this datacentre egress, on every path including the XML API: Islington, Kingston, Lewisham, Merton, Sutton, Tower Hamlets, Waltham Forest and Westminster. That is one shared Azure Front Door WAF rule, not eight separate decisions, so a single change of egress (UK residential IP, or a real browser) would likely unblock all eight at once. Kensington and Chelsea is blocked separately by Cloudflare. The other seven committee sites were reachable with plain curl.

national_fallback.why: MHCLG collects a service-level revenue budget (RA) and capital estimates (CER) return from every English council, including all 16 boroughs here, and publishes them as per-authority ODS. Where a borough is PDF-only, this is the structured substitute for the service-line figures, at the cost of MHCLG's service classification rather than the council's own directorate names.
